Title: National service training draws encouraging response as 10 turn up without prior confirmation
Article:
ALOR STAR: The response to the National Service Training Programme 3.0 (NS 3.0) has been encouraging, with 10 people voluntarily turning up at the 513th Regiment (Territorial Army) National Service Training Camp in Kepala Batas here today, despite not having confirmed their participation in advance.
Colonel Abdul Rani Abdul Majid, director of the Policy and Development Division at the National Service Training Department headquarters, said the development indicated that some individuals were interested in joining NS 3.0 after learning more about the programme.
"We received confirmation from 211 trainees who were scheduled to register today. In addition, 10 people arrived voluntarily this morning without prior confirmation to apply for the training," he said while observing the registration of NS 3.0 Series 4/2026 trainees here today.
He said the 211 trainees who had confirmed their participation were scheduled to register at the camp, with the training curriculum comprising 70 per cent military modules and 30 per cent nation-building modules.
Abdul Rani also encouraged parents to support their children in joining NS 3.0, citing positive feedback from evaluations conducted with trainees' parents.
He added that one of the benefits of participating in NS was that trainees who completed the programme would earn specific merit points from five appointing authorities, giving them an advantage when applying for relevant services.
The five appointing authorities are the Public Services Commission, Armed Forces Council, Police Force Commission, Judicial and Legal Service Commission, and authorities related to the public service.
Meanwhile, National Service Training Department director-general Major General Datuk Marzuki Mokhtar said an evaluation of the NS 3.0 implementation showed a high level of parental satisfaction, with all six key elements recording positive feedback of more than 90 per cent.
He said the validation exercise, conducted by the National Service Training Department in collaboration with Sultan Idris Education University (UPSI), involved 571 respondents out of 4,199 parents of trainees from previous series.
"Overall, the six elements recorded an average of 95.55 per cent for the combined 'Strongly Agree' and 'Agree' responses. The effectiveness of NS 3.0 achieved the highest score at 97.98 per cent, followed by discipline and personal transformation at 97.79 per cent," he said.
Marzuki added that the increase in the number of trainees confirming their attendance for Series 4/2026 demonstrated an encouraging response, with 2,009 trainees confirming that they would report for duty today at eight camps nationwide, surpassing the target of 1,203 trainees.
He said the development indicated that NS 3.0 was gaining traction within the community, particularly among parents who viewed the programme as a platform to shape the character, discipline, resilience, unity and sense of responsibility of the younger generation.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Political journeyman Norhizam ready for another Melaka run
Article:
MELAKA: Former Pengkalan Batu assemblyman Datuk Norhizam Hassan Baktee says he is ready to contest in the upcoming state election.
The Hang Tuah Jaya Bersatu vice-chief said this included the possibility of contesting his former seat.
"I will contest, though I'm not sure which seat. I am open to being fielded anywhere if that is the party's decision.
"But I want to serve the people of Pengkalan Batu again," he said when contacted.
He claimed voters in the area had expressed hope that he could serve as their assemblyman again.
Addressing a poster about his "comeback" that went viral on social media, Norhizam said he did not know who circulated it.
"I appreciate the support from the people for me to contest.
"As long as Pengkalan Batu needs a brave and firm leader, I am always ready to serve."
Norhizam, who began his political career with Umno before switching to DAP, served as Pengkalan Batu assemblyman after winning the seat in the 14th general election.
In 2020, he quit DAP to become an independent assemblyman and later tried to defend the seat in the 2021 Melaka election.
He contested as an independent but secured only 1,218 votes, losing his deposit.
The seat was won by Barisan Nasional's Datuk Kalsom Noordin.
In 2024, Norhizam revealed that he had joined Bersatu.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: [UPDATED] MACC seizes 25 luxury vehicles worth RM25mil in tax reduction probe
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) has seized 25 luxury vehicles worth about RM25 million in connection with an investigation into a company manager suspected of submitting false documents to obtain tax reductions worth about RM200 million.
The vehicles were seized during searches at 12 locations, comprising office premises and the suspect's residences. MACC also froze four personal bank accounts and three company accounts containing about RM3 million.
MACC has also obtained a three-day extension of the remand order against the man, in his 40s, from Oct 4 to 6.
The extension was granted by Magistrate Illya Syaheedah Mohd Razif at the magistrate's court here today following an application by MACC after the suspect's initial remand period expired today.
The suspect, a company manager at a financial and corporate services agency, is being investigated over allegations of submitting false documents to obtain tax reductions worth about RM200 million.
He was arrested on Sept 30 when he appeared at MACC headquarters to have his statement recorded.
Preliminary investigations revealed that the suspect allegedly committed the offence between 2018 and 2026.
The suspect is also believed to have bribed an enforcement agency officer and manipulated about 480 company accounts using false documents to secure the tax reduction, while allegedly amassing wealth through the activities.
MACC Chief Commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman had previously confirmed that the case was being investigated under Section 16 of the MACC Act 2009.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Umno ready to discuss Pas' use of BN logo in Melaka polls
Article:
KOTA TINGGI: Umno is prepared to discuss Pas' intention to use the Barisan Nasional logo in the upcoming Melaka election.
Umno vice-president Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said the party welcomed the intention, but any such proposal would have to be discussed through official channels.
"If that is what they want, we are prepared to discuss it. But that does not mean we have met. Since he said it to the media, I am responding through the media as well.
"If any party is prepared to contest using the BN logo, we very much welcome it. But this must be based on the fundamental decision," he said at a press conference after attending the groundbreaking ceremony for the Kota Tinggi Muslim Orphanage here today.
Khaled, who is also the Kota Tinggi member of Parliament, was commenting on a statement by Pas deputy president Datuk Seri Tuan Ibrahim Tuan Man, who indicated that the party was prepared to use the BN logo if it could not use the Perikatan Nasional (PN) logo.
Asked whether other PN component parties, such as Parti Wawasan Negara (Wawasan), would also want to use the BN logo, Khaled jokingly said the openness did not extend to every party.
"Those who want to come to our house, they are people we like. Not everyone," he said.
Meanwhile, Khaled declined to comment further on the allocation of seats for the Melaka election, saying he was not directly involved in the matter.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Man jailed seven years for misappropriating RM254,000 in company funds
Article:
MIRI: A man was sentenced to seven years in jail, fined RM20,000 and ordered to receive one stroke of the rotan after pleading guilty to misappropriating more than RM254,000 in company funds.
Miri police chief Assistant Commissioner Mohd Farhan Lee Abdullah said the 36-year-old man, who worked for the company, was entrusted with the money on Sept 18.
The money was meant for workers' wages in Lapok, Long Jeeh and Bario.
"Instead of paying the staff, the man used the funds for personal expenses, including online gambling," Farhan said in a statement.
The employer later lodged a police report and the man was arrested on Sept 23.
"Police recovered RM10,850 in cash and a Toyota Hilux belonging to the company," he said.
The man was charged in the Miri Sessions Court and sentenced on Oct 1 following his guilty plea.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malbatt peacekeepers  in Lebanon to return home from January 2027
Article:
KOTA TINGGI: All members of the Malaysian Battalion (Malbatt) currently serving in Lebanon are expected to begin returning home in January 2027, following the conclusion of the United Nations Interim Force in Lebanon (Unifil) mandate at the end of this year.
Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said the withdrawal process would be carried out in stages via several flights, followed by the return of military assets by sea starting Jan 17.
He said all battalions operating in Lebanon were scheduled to complete their respective deployments by the end of December, in line with the expiration of the mission's mandate.
"Our personnel are expected to start returning next January on several flights, while Malaysian military assets will be brought back by ship starting Jan 17," he said at a press conference following the groundbreaking ceremony for the Kota Tinggi Muslim Orphanage here today.
In a related development, Khaled said Malaysia was prepared to consider participating in a new peacekeeping force in Lebanon should the United Nations (UN) request it.
However, he said this readiness was subject to the UN's decision and the mandate provided, as Malaysia would not participate in any military operation that did not fall under the mandate of the world body.
"If the UN decides to establish a new force under whatever name and requires our involvement, Malaysia is prepared to participate.
"However, this is subject to the UN's decision. We will not participate in any operation that does not fall under the mandate of the relevant world body," he said.
Khaled said the matter was also addressed during his recent working visit to Lebanon, including in discussions with his counterpart, who indicated that the security situation in the country remained volatile and exposed to various threats.
He noted that a UN conference was currently underway, and many of the countries participating in the peacekeeping mission had expressed the view that the mission's termination should be reviewed.
Recounting the history of Malaysia's involvement in Lebanon, Khaled said Malaysian military participation began on a small scale in 2007 before the UN approved a full battalion-strength deployment in 2013.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Doctor couple lose RM300k after being duped by father of former singer
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A doctor couple allegedly lost RM300,000 after being duped into investing in the Kad Prihatin Siswa project by a Datuk who promised them lucrative returns.
The man, who is also the father of a former singer, allegedly told the couple that 620,000 students from 20 universities would benefit from the project through a collaboration with a well-known telecommunications company.
The victim, who wished to be known as Dr Alia, 38, said the man claimed to have connections with senior government officials and told them that minutes of meetings on the project had been submitted to the government.
The man also claimed that the project was being implemented across Peninsular Malaysia, Sabah and Sarawak, while promising investors returns and annual trips to London or umrah in business class.
Dr Alia said she knew the Datuk as the son-in-law of one of her patients. She added that the man had previously visited her clinic and asked her to make a house call to treat his mother-in-law.
"Since then, my husband and I became close to him as I treated his mother-in-law until she passed away.
"He also invited us to his Hari Raya open house and we remained close after that.
"He would often invite us out for drinks at weekends before telling us about his business, projects with the government and influential connections, including senior government officials," she said when contacted.
Dr Alia said the man eventually persuaded her husband to join his team for the Kad Prihatin Siswa project, claiming that he believed in him and wanted to help him become more successful and wealthy.
She said the couple invested RM300,000 in the project in August 2023.
"He also sent us photographs of himself in meetings with a telecommunications company and a bank regarding the project," she said.
She said the man had also shown her a letter which he claimed had been minuted to the Deputy Prime Minister.
"To this day, I am not sure whether the project actually exists. He claimed that he wanted to help Malay youths share in the prosperity.
"We only realised we had been deceived when he (the Datuk) asked us to increase our investment and pressured us to put in more money," she said.
Dr Alia said the couple had yet to receive any returns from the investment. She later lodged a police report at the Ampang police station last Wednesday.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Immigration arrests 37,313 undocumented migrants in nine months
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The Immigration Department carried out 10,374 enforcement operations nationwide and arrested 37,313 undocumented migrants between Jan 1 and Sept 29 this year.
Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said 137,603 people were screened during the operations as part of the ministry's enforcement against immigration offences.
He said enforcement also targeted employers suspected of hiring or harbouring undocumented migrants.
"A total of 1,809 employers were arrested during the period, 1,692 of whom were Malaysians," he said in a social media post today.
Saifuddin said the figures reflected the ministry's approach of targeting not only undocumented migrants but also those who employed and harboured them.
He said employer arrests had risen substantially from 346 in 2023 to 1,859 in 2024 and 2,202 last year.
For the first nine months of this year, 1,809 employers had already been arrested.
"Enforcement cannot only focus on undocumented migrants. It must also reach those who employ and harbour them," he said.
Saifuddin said the Home Ministry and Immigration Department would continue conducting enforcement operations daily.
He described undocumented migrants as a longstanding problem aggravated by weaknesses and leakages in the system, exploited by syndicates and irresponsible employers.
Saifuddin said he wanted the ministry and Immigration Department to adopt a proactive enforcement approach rather than respond only when cases attracted public attention.
"This is not seasonal enforcement and it is not carried out only when an issue becomes the focus of attention.
"The Home Ministry and Immigration will continue to break this chain of abuse to safeguard the country's sovereignty and security," he said.
He also warned foreigners entering Malaysia to use legal channels and comply with immigration laws, saying action would be taken against those involved in illegal entry, document forgery or overstaying.
Employers, meanwhile, were warned against hiring or harbouring undocumented migrants.
Saifuddin also urged Malaysians not to harbour undocumented migrants and to cooperate with the authorities in dealing with immigration offences.
The Immigration Department has said its enforcement operations are conducted throughout the year and are not limited to foreign nationals, adding that employers and property owners were also liable for action if they breached immigration laws.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Sultan of Brunei arrives as Sepang hosts surprise F1 GP
Article:
SUBANG JAYA, Oct 3 — The Sultan of Brunei, Sultan Hassanal Bolkiah, arrived in Malaysia today for a special visit in conjunction with the Formula 1 (F1) Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix (GP) at the Sepang International Circuit (SIC), which began yesterday.
The special aircraft carrying His Majesty and the Brunei delegation, including Prince Abdul Mateen Bolkiah, landed safely at the Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF) base in Subang at 4.28pm.
They were welcomed by Tunku Temenggong Johor Tunku Idris Iskandar Al-Haj Sultan Ibrahim and Minister of Youth and Sports Dr Mohammed Taufiq Johari.
His Majesty then inspected a guard of honour comprising two officers and 26 personnel of other ranks from the First Battalion of the Royal Malay Regiment, led by Captain Wan Amirul Syafiq Wan Zamri.
The Sepang International Circuit has been selected to host the 2026 F1 Gulf Air Bahrain GP, making the iconic circuit a temporary venue for the prestigious race.
Last July, Formula 1 confirmed that Malaysia would host the race, which is taking place until this Sunday.
This follows an agreement reached between Formula 1, the International Automobile Federation (FIA), and the governments of Malaysia and Bahrain.
The agreement ensures the Bahrain GP remains on the 2026 F1 calendar after the race was cancelled earlier this season due to geopolitical tensions in West Asia.
Malaysia previously hosted the Malaysian GP at Sepang from 1999 to 2017 before being dropped from the F1 calendar.
The return of the race to Malaysia is the result of diplomatic efforts involving His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, and King Hamad Isa Al-Khalifa of Bahrain. — Bernama

Title: Manager held three more days over alleged RM200m tax reduction fraud
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 3 — A financial and corporate services company manager has had his remand extended for another three days from tomorrow to assist in the investigation into the submission of documents containing false information to obtain a tax reduction worth approximately RM200 million.
The remand order against the man in his 40s was issued by Magistrate Illya Syaheedah Mohd Razif after the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) applied for the extension at the Putrajaya Magistrate’s Court today.
The suspect will be remanded until October 6, after his initial three-day remand period, which began last Thursday, ended today.
The media previously reported that preliminary investigations found the suspect was believed to have manipulated approximately 480 company accounts using fraudulent documents between 2018 and this year.
The man is also believed to have bribed an enforcement agency official to facilitate his activities, in addition to allegedly accumulating extraordinary wealth through the illicit operations.
Further investigations by the MACC led to raids at 12 locations, including the suspect’s office and residential premises.
During the operation, the MACC seized 25 luxury vehicles estimated to be worth approximately RM25 million.
The MACC also froze seven bank accounts, comprising four personal accounts and three company accounts, with a total value of approximately RM3 million.
MACC Chief Commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman, when contacted, confirmed the remand extension and said the case is being investigated under Section 16 of the MACC Act 2009. — Bernama

Title: Melaka polls: Pakatan to announce candidates in one or two weeks, says Amirudin
Article:
KLANG, Oct 3 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) is expected to announce its candidates for the Melaka state election within the next one or two weeks, says PH election director Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari.
He said the coalition’s election machinery preparations have been progressing smoothly over the past two months.
“Our machinery is moving and ready. It is only the coordination, alignment, and mutual understanding that are yet to be finalised.
“God willing, in the near future — within a week or two — we will announce the candidates who will be contesting,” he said when met at the launch of the Tabung Warisan Anak Selangor (Tawas) ‘Tuaian Anak Harapan’ (Tuah) Initiative at the KSL Convention Centre here today.
On September 27, Melaka PH confirmed that seat distribution among its component parties at the state level for the Melaka state election had been completed.
Melaka PH chairman Adly Zahari was reported as saying that the final seat arrangement, however, would be concluded following discussions among the PH Presidential Council, state PH leadership, and Amirudin as PH election director.
Meanwhile, asked about PH’s cooperation with Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia (Bersatu) for the state election, Amirudin, who is also Selangor Menteri Besar, said PH remains open to discussions if there is room for such collaboration.
“If there is room, we will discuss. If not, we are ready to contest based on our existing capacity and understanding,” he said.
Melaka Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh previously announced that the state legislative assembly was dissolved effective September 23 after obtaining the consent of Melaka Yang Dipertua Negeri Tun Mohd Ali Mohd Rustam. — Bernama

Title: Time for a review: Creative industry seeks more Budget 2027 support as TV production rates lag behind costs
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 3 — Creative industry players are calling on the government to maintain and enhance existing funds and incentives in the upcoming Budget 2027, while reviewing television programme production rates, which they say are no longer realistic amid rising costs.
Malaysian Film Producers Association deputy president Datuk Dr Yusof Haslam said government incentives and assistance should be maintained without cuts to safeguard the sustainability of the local creative industry ecosystem.
“I hope the government will look at this from a positive perspective and maintain all the assistance that has been provided to the industry. If there are plans for cuts, I hope they can be avoided,” he said when he appeared as a guest on Bernama TV’s ‘On E’ programme at Wisma Bernama here today.
Yusof also reminded industry players to uphold their responsibilities and integrity when managing any grant or allocation received from the government.
“Filmmakers must complete their films within the allocated budget and take the work seriously. These funds should not be used as a platform to make money for personal gain,” he said.
On the Film in Malaysia Incentive (FIMI), Yusof said the initiative has not only succeeded in attracting international production companies but has also provided crucial support for large-scale patriotic productions such as ‘MALBATT: Misi Bakara’.
He also appealed for television programme production rates, particularly those offered by Radio Televisyen Malaysia (RTM), to be reviewed in line with current cost increases, saying there had been no significant adjustment for almost four decades.
“I have been producing television dramas since 1985. At that time, the cost of a TV drama was within RM40,000. But after 40 years, the increase (in RTM’s payment) has only been about RM10,000.
“These rates should be reviewed every 10 years because if RTM increases its rates, other private companies will follow suit,” he said.
Meanwhile, film producer Nazira Ibrahim said the creative sector is a comprehensive ecosystem that requires consistent support, particularly in film marketing and distribution, to assist smaller-scale productions.
“Sometimes we have good products and compelling stories, but we have no avenue to market and distribute them to audiences. If the government can assist in developing these mechanisms, it could significantly raise the profile of our films and help them reach both local and international audiences,” she said.
On the RM10 million allocation for TVET Madani Creative Multimedia programmes, Nazira called for practical training on film sets to be prioritised over theoretical learning to produce highly skilled technical personnel behind the scenes.
“Skills are needed not only for those in front of the camera, such as the actors, scriptwriters and directors, but are equally important for people working behind the scenes, including camera operators, lighting crews and those handling visual effects, post-production and sound systems.
“Theoretical exposure alone is not enough. Students need industry training with production companies and should be exposed to actual film sets to see firsthand how a production operates,” she said.
Under Budget 2026, the government allocated RM110 million in incentives to encourage local and international film producers to create high-quality productions in Malaysia.
The initiative included a dedicated RM10 million allocation for the production of nation-building content as part of efforts to strengthen the orange economy ecosystem.
Budget 2027 is scheduled to be tabled in Parliament on October 9. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia cuts use of ozone-depleting HCFC by nearly 80pc, eyes full phase-out by 2030
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 3 — The National World Ozone Day 2026 celebration has reinforced Malaysia’s commitment to protecting the ozone layer and tackling climate change through a transition towards more sustainable and energy-efficient cooling technologies.
In a statement today, the Department of Environment (DOE) said the celebration, officiated by DOE Deputy Director-General (Development) Azuri Azizah Saedon at a shopping centre here, carried the theme “Global Action for a Cooler Planet: Celebrating 10 Years of Sustainable Cooling under the Kigali Amendment to the Montreal Protocol”.
“This theme marks a decade of the Kigali Amendment, which focuses on reducing the consumption of high global warming potential hydrofluorocarbons (HFCs), alongside accelerating the transition to sustainable and energy-efficient cooling technology.
“Malaysia, which ratified the Montreal Protocol in 1989, completely phased out chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs) and Halons in 2010.
“The nation has also reduced its hydrochlorofluorocarbons (HCFCs) consumption by nearly 80 per cent, aiming for a complete phase-out by 2030 under Stage III of the HCFC Phase-out Management Plan (HPMP III) and Stage I of the Kigali Implementation Plan,” the DOE said.
The DOE noted that these achievements stem from continuous collaboration between the government, industry, international development partners, relevant institutions, and the public to ensure Malaysia’s obligations under the Montreal Protocol and Kigali Amendment are effectively fulfilled.
Meanwhile, the DOE highlighted that Malaysia continues to strengthen environmental sustainability through a Refrigerant Lifecycle Management (RLM) approach to prevent harmful gas emissions and stimulate the circular economy.
“The DOE is also enhancing governance and industry competency by upgrading policies, legislation, and technical guidance for technicians. However, the implementation of the Montreal Protocol and Kigali Amendment demands a comprehensive commitment from industry, training institutes, the public, and key stakeholders,” the statement read.
Consequently, the DOE urged members of the public to play their part by selecting eco-friendly and energy-efficient cooling appliances, engaging DOE-certified technicians for maintenance services, ensuring the proper disposal of refrigerants, and consistently practising energy conservation.
The department affirmed it will continue ensuring policies, plans, and strategies related to the HCFC phase-out and HFC phase-down are effectively executed, alongside reinforcing legal frameworks, compliance, and enforcement regarding refrigerants in line with technological developments and Malaysia’s obligations under the Montreal Protocol.
“The 2026 World Ozone Day celebration does not merely commemorate past achievements; it serves as an ongoing reminder that efforts to safeguard the ozone layer and combat climate change must be sustained to secure a cleaner, healthier, and more sustainable environment for future generations,” the statement added.
World Ozone Day is celebrated annually on September 16 to commemorate the signing of the Montreal Protocol on Substances that Deplete the Ozone Layer in 1987, as well as to raise public awareness on the importance of protecting the ozone layer and addressing climate change. — Bernama

Title: Police arrest motorcyclist for riding against traffic, crashing into two KL marathon participants
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 3 — A 21-year-old motorcyclist was arrested after allegedly riding against traffic and crashing into two participants of the Kuala Lumpur Standard Chartered Marathon (KLSCM) 2026 along Jalan Munshi Abdullah early today.
Kuala Lumpur Traffic Investigation and Enforcement Department chief ACP Mohd Zamzuri Mohd Isa said the incident occurred at about 6.15am after the motorcyclist, who was carrying a 19-year-old pillion rider, allegedly passed through a road closure marked by cones.
“The rider was ordered to stop by police personnel manning the road closure, but is believed to have fled by riding against the flow of traffic before crashing into two marathon participants who were running,” he said in a press statement.
One participant, a 50-year-old woman, suffered neck injuries and is receiving treatment at Prince Court.
The other victim, a 41-year-old man, sustained injuries to his right knee and hand.
Mohd Zamzuri said an initial alcohol screening on the motorcyclist returned a positive result, with an evidential breath alcohol reading of 164mg/100ml.
The motorcyclist and pillion rider were subsequently taken to Hospital Kuala Lumpur for blood and urine samples as part of further investigations.
The case is being investigated under Section 44(1A)(b) of the Road Transport Act 1987 and Section 186 of the Penal Code.
The motorcyclist has been remanded for three days from today until October 5, while the pillion rider has been remanded for two days until October 4, with both being held at the Dang Wangi police station lock-up.
Police urged witnesses or anyone with information on the incident to contact the Tun H.S. Lee Traffic Police Station at 03-2071 9999 or the nearest police station.

Title: Family of Bandar Utama school stabbing victim files civil suit against government agencies, boy and his parents
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 3 — The mother and sister of the 16-year-old student who was fatally stabbed at a secondary school in Bandar Utama last year have filed a civil suit at the Kuala Lumpur High Court.
The family’s lawyer, Surendra Ananth, confirmed the suit that was filed on Thursday, adding that case management has been fixed for October 29.
“We have named a number of government agencies as defendants. We have named the parents of the boy who killed my daughter as defendants. We have also named the boy himself as a defendant,” the victim's mother, Wong Lee Ping, said in a statement today.
“With the increasing mental health challenges faced by our children today, we cannot choose to stay silent anymore.
“Grand statements and plans are insufficient. We cannot wait until more lives are lost before proper action is taken,” she added.
The intention to pursue civil action was first publicly announced on by Wong September.
Almost a year after her daughter, Yap Shing Xuen, was fatally stabbed on October 14 last year, Wong continues to seek answers over whether the tragedy could have been prevented.
At the time, the family said it planned to pursue a civil suit as the criminal case moved to the appeal stage following the Shah Alam High Court’s decision to acquit the teenage accused on the grounds of unsoundness of mind.
“Our lawyers will be filing a civil suit. Until the criminal proceedings are completed, we will not comment on the details. Our lawyers will explain those matters later,” Wong told a press conference on September 25.
The teenager accused of killing Yap, who was 14 at the time, was charged with murder at the Petaling Jaya Magistrates’ Court on October 22 last year.
The case subsequently underwent psychiatric assessment before being transferred to the Shah Alam High Court, where the trial was conducted in camera as the accused was a minor.
A psychiatric assessment found him fit to stand trial in January. He pleaded not guilty when the murder charge was read again at the High Court on February 12.
The trial began on August 3. On August 13, the High Court ordered the teenager to enter his defence after finding that the prosecution had established a
prima facie
case.
The defence closed its case on August 26 after two witnesses — the accused and a forensic psychiatrist — testified.
On September 14, High Court Judge Adlin Abdul Majid acquitted and discharged the teenager after finding that he was of unsound mind at the time of the offence, and ordered him to be placed at Hospital Bahagia Ulu Kinta for a period to be approved by the Sultan of Selangor.
The Attorney General’s Chambers filed a notice of appeal at the Court of Appeal on September 22, challenging the acquittal.

Title: Malaysian pilot detained in Jakarta over alleged drug smuggling gets another 30 days in custody
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 3 — The 39-year-old Malaysia Airlines pilot arrested in Jakarta in July over an alleged drug-smuggling operation remains in Indonesian custody after authorities extended his detention beyond the initial 60-day period.
Harian Metro
reported today that Bukit Aman Narcotics Crime Investigation Department director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said the extension was for another 30 days.
“The Malaysian police were informed by the Indonesian narcotics authorities. The case is still at the investigation and assessment stage,” he was quoted as saying.
He added that the detention could be extended for a further 30 days, based on information provided by Indonesian authorities.
Meanwhile, another pilot and six other individuals arrested in Malaysia over alleged links to the same drug syndicate have been detained for 60 days under the Dangerous Drugs (Special Preventive Measures) Act 1985.
The investigation centres on allegations that the suspects were linked to drug-smuggling activities spanning Malaysia and Indonesia.
The Malaysia Airlines pilot was arrested at Jakarta’s Soekarno-Hatta International Airport in July after Indonesian authorities reportedly seized 15 packages containing about 70,000 capsules suspected to contain ecstasy and methamphetamine, weighing about 25kg in total.

Title: Sepang International Circuit working with partners, authorities to improve F1 traffic management
Article:
SEPANG, Oct 3 — The Sepang International Circuit (SIC) is working closely with its transport partners and relevant authorities to strengthen traffic, shuttle and crowd management arrangements for the Formula 1 (F1) Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix (GP) 2026 race.
SIC said the measures followed challenges experienced by some fans travelling to and from the circuit yesterday, particularly during the evening departure period.
“The experience and safety of our fans remain our highest priority at Sepang International Circuit,” it said in a statement today.
The circuit operator advised fans attending the weekend race to plan their journeys in advance and refer to the latest travel information on its official social media channels.
A Formula 1 driver is seen during the free practice session for the Formula 1 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix at the Sepang International Circuit October 2, 2026. — Bernama pic
Fans arriving at or departing from the circuit are also advised to follow the directions of officials and on-ground signage, as traffic arrangements may be adjusted according to prevailing conditions.
SIC thanked fans for their patience and cooperation, adding that it looked forward to welcoming them for an enjoyable and safe day at the circuit.
Yesterday, several ticket holders took to social media to voice their frustration over severe gridlock when exiting the circuit, with some reporting lengthy waits for shuttle buses connecting parking areas and public transport hubs.
In July, Formula 1 confirmed that Malaysia would host the Gulf Air Bahrain GP from October 2 to 4, following an agreement involving Formula 1, the Fédération Internationale de l’Automobile (FIA), and the governments of Malaysia and Bahrain.
The agreement keeps the Bahrain GP on the 2026 F1 calendar after the race was cancelled earlier this season due to geopolitical tensions in West Asia. — Bernama

Title: Military build-up on Philippine island risks conflict spillover to nearby Malaysia, says Khaled Nordin
Article:
KOTA TINGGI, Oct 3 — Malaysia does not view the military build-up on the southern Philippine island of Balabac as a direct threat, said Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin.
The defence minister said it was the Philippines’ right and prerogative to cooperate with the US military to strengthen its defence capabilities.
“For us, it is not the military buildup on Balabac Island itself that worries us, but rather its proximity to Malaysia.
“Should any dispute or conflict occur, even a minor one in geopolitical terms, the repercussions could spill over into Malaysia,” he told reporters after officiating the groundbreaking ceremony for an Islamic orphanage here today.
On a separate matter, Mohamed Khaled said the government aims to achieve a 50-50 ratio in the deployment of Malaysian Armed Forces (MAF) personnel between Peninsular Malaysia and Sabah and Sarawak.
He said the move was intended to ensure a more balanced national defence posture.
At present, about two-thirds of MAF personnel are stationed in Peninsular Malaysia, with the remainder based in Sabah and Sarawak.
Mohamed Khaled said there are about 20,000 active MAF personnel in Sabah and Sarawak at any one time.
“We aim for a balanced deployment based on the 50-50 ratio.
“This is part of the national defense strategy, while taking into account of Sabah and Sarawak’s geographical proximity to areas where conflicts could potentially arise,” he said, adding that defence readiness must be enhanced to address any potential conflict, confrontation or provocation in the region.
Balabac Island is one of nine Philippine sites covered by the Philippines-US Enhanced Defence Cooperation Agreement (EDCA), which allows rotational access by US forces for activities including joint training and exercises.
The island is about 50 kilometres from Sabah’s Pulau Banggi, and increased military activity there has drawn attention in Malaysia amid wider geopolitical tensions in the South China Sea and the Philippines’ longstanding claim over Sabah, which Malaysia rejects.

Title: Premier: Sarawak Budget 2027 to cover electricity tariffs, revenue and economic direction
Article:
MUKAH, Oct 3 — Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Openg hinted that the Sarawak Budget 2027, to be tabled at the upcoming State Legislative Assembly (DUN) session, will address various matters, including electricity tariffs, economic direction, and the state’s revenue position.
However, he did not elaborate on the measures to be announced, asking the public instead to await the budget presentation.
“God willing, I will table the Sarawak Budget in two weeks. Let us wait for the budget.
“Other states have raised electricity tariffs. As for whether Sarawak will raise them... do not worry, as long as Abang Johari is here,” he said while officiating the Sarawakku Sayang 2026 Programme (Mukah Division) at Dataran Pehin Setia Raja here today.
Abang Johari also gave an indication regarding Sarawak’s economic direction and the state’s revenue position, details of which will be provided during the presentation.
“What about our economic direction for the future of our children? Do not worry... the future is bright. And what about Sarawak’s revenue? Is it up or down? Wait for the 12th (of October),” he said.
Meanwhile, Abang Johari said Sarawak would not back down in defending its rights to oil and gas resources, ensuring that the wealth generated is utilised to fund development and improve the people’s well-being.
He noted that this stance is based on Sarawak’s rights as enshrined in the Malaysia Agreement 1963 (MA63).
“I will not back down regarding Sarawak’s rights to oil and gas. We must optimise our natural resources so that the returns can be channeled back to the people of Sarawak,” he said.
Abang Johari said state revenue is required to fund various development needs, including the construction of roads and infrastructure, as well as the development of the agricultural sector.
He noted that the establishment of Petroleum Sarawak Berhad (Petros) is one of the state government’s strategic measures to manage oil and gas resources. — Bernama

Title: No more RM12.50 medicine delivery fee, but for rural Sabah patients, the bigger savings may be the journey
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Oct 3 — Sabah patients using the Ubat Melalui Pos (UMP) service no longer have to pay the RM12.50 delivery charge from October 1 removing a cost that was more than twice the RM5.70 previously charged in Peninsular Malaysia.
Particularly meaningful in Sabah, where patients from rural and interior areas have to travel considerable distances simply to collect repeat medication from hospitals or health clinics.
About 87,000 registered UMP patients nationwide are expected to benefit from the free delivery initiative.
Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the Government would bear the delivery cost beginning October 1, with an initial RM5 million allocation considered through the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC).
The free delivery initiative took effect on October 1 and is aimed at ensuring patients in all states can benefit from the service.
Previously, patients had to bear the delivery cost, which was RM5.70 in Peninsular Malaysia and RM12.50 in Sabah and Sarawak.
Health Minister Datuk Seri Dzulkefly Ahmad said the initiative was particularly relevant to people in rural areas, who often have to travel long distances to health facilities merely to collect their medicines.
Besides reducing patients’ expenses and travelling time, he said the medicine delivery service could help ensure continuity of treatment and reduce congestion at government health facilities.
Under UMP, eligible patients can have their repeat medication delivered to a preferred location instead of returning to a pharmacy counter for every supply.
The service forms part of the Ministry of Health’s efforts to provide more patient-centred healthcare, particularly for elderly patients, working people and others who may face difficulties travelling repeatedly to health facilities.
UMP has been implemented in cooperation with Pos Malaysia since 2011. In Sabah, the service is already available at several Ministry of Health facilities.
The current MyUBAT directory lists UMP among the services available at Queen Elizabeth Hospital, Queen Elizabeth II Hospital, Hospital Ranau, Hospital Semporna, Hospital Sipitang, Hospital Tambunan and Hospital Tawau.
This means patients receiving eligible repeat prescriptions from participating facilities may be able to obtain subsequent supplies without making another trip solely to collect their medication.
For rural patients in Sabah, the savings could extend beyond the RM12.50 delivery charge, particularly where a hospital visit involves fuel costs, public transport fares, time away from work or assistance from family members.
However, access in Sabah’s most remote settlements may still depend on delivery coverage available at the patient’s address.
For example, Queen Elizabeth II Hospital’s pharmacy operating policy states that addresses for UMP delivery must fall within Pos Laju’s coverage area.
The policy also states that psychotropic or dangerous drugs, extemporaneous preparations and medicines requiring special storage cannot be supplied through the service.
Further clarification is being sought on the number of Sabah patients currently using UMP, how many are expected to benefit from the free delivery initiative and the extent to which the service reaches remote and interior villages.
Patients can manage repeat medicine supplies through MyUBAT, which enables participating Ministry of Health facilities to provide services including medicine-by-post.
The Government has also reminded patients to use official channels rather than social media accounts when registering for UMP services. — Daily Express

Title: Young Malaysians show enthusiasm as PLKN 3.0 attracts ten unexpected volunteers in Kepala Batas
Article:
ALOR SETAR, Oct 3 — The response to the National Service Training Programme (PLKN) 3.0 has been encouraging, with 10 individuals voluntarily showing up at the 513th Regiment (Territorial Army) National Service Training Camp (CLKN) in Kepala Batas here today, despite not having made prior confirmation to join the programme.
Colonel Abdul Rani Abdul Majid, director of the Policy and Development Division at the National Service Training Department (JLKN) headquarters, said this development indicates there are individuals interested in joining PLKN 3.0 after learning about the programme.
“We had received confirmation from 211 trainees scheduled to register today, additionally, as of this morning, 10 people arrived voluntarily without prior confirmation to apply for the training,” he told Bernama while observing the registration for PLKN 3.0 Series 4/2026 trainees here today.
He noted that the 211 trainees who had confirmed their participation were scheduled to register at the camp, with the training curriculum comprising 70 per cent military modules and 30 per cent nation-building modules.
Abdul Rani also encouraged parents to support their children in joining PLKN 3.0, citing the positive feedback received through evaluations conducted with the trainees’ parents.
He added that one of the benefits of participating in PLKN is that trainees who complete the programme will earn specific merit points from five appointing authorities, thereby gaining an advantage when applying for relevant services.
The five appointing authorities are the Public Services Commission, the Armed Forces Council, the Police Force Commission, the Judicial and Legal Service Commission, and authorities related to the public service.
Meanwhile, National Service Training Department (JLKN) director-general, Major General Datuk Marzuki Mokhtar, said the evaluation of the PLKN 3.0 implementation revealed a high level of parental satisfaction, with all six key elements recording positive feedback exceeding 90 per cent.
He noted that the validation findings, conducted by JLKN in collaboration with Sultan Idris Education University (UPSI), involved 571 respondents out of 4,199 parents of trainees from previous series.
“Overall, the six elements recorded an average of 95.55 per cent for the combined ‘Strongly Agree’ and ‘Agree’ responses; the effectiveness of PLKN 3.0 achieved the highest score at 97.98 per cent, followed by discipline and personal transformation at 97.79 per cent,” he said.
Marzuki added that the increase in the number of trainees confirming their attendance for Series 4/2026 demonstrated an encouraging response, with 2,009 trainees confirming they would report for duty today at eight camps nationwide, surpassing the target of 1,203 trainees.
He said this development indicates PLKN 3.0 is gaining traction within the community—particularly among parents who view the programme as a platform to shape the character, discipline, resilience, unity, and sense of responsibility of the younger generation. — Bernama

Title: ‘Use official complaints channel’: Fahmi urges public to report ethical media concerns to Malaysian Media Council
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Oct 3 — Members of the public who have complaints regarding the ethics of local media reporting can channel them to the Malaysian Media Council (MMM), said Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil.
He said any grievances should be channelled through the proper avenues to avoid misunderstandings and actions that could affect the integrity and credibility of the media industry.
“If it concerns reporting by the media itself, I would suggest that members of the public, who have concerns about a news headline or anything they wish to raise with the media, use the official complaints channel through the MMM. There is a link that can be accessed,” he said.
He said this after officiating the Madani Kita Programme with the Kota Anggerik @ Shah Alam community here today.
Yesterday, the Putrajaya Media Club (KMP) lodged reports with police and the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) regarding a social media post that allegedly edited images of media personnel into images of animals.
The irresponsible act involved photographs of a group of photographers and journalists covering former Prime Minister Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad’s visit to the grave of his wife, Tun Dr Siti Hasmah Mohd Ali, at Pusara Negara, Putrajaya, on Thursday (Oct 1).
Elaborating, Fahmi said MCMC had identified several social media accounts found to have disseminated offensive content by misusing artificial intelligence (AI) applications to edit images of Tun Dr Mahathir during the period following Tun Dr Siti Hasmah’s passing.
“The authorities will take action. I personally noticed that the account has disappeared. We are not yet sure whether it was a fake account, but the MCMC, together with the police, is tracking down the parties responsible for producing extremely offensive content in this matter.
“To members of the media, I would also like to offer a reminder that we should give space and respect the family’s wishes while they are grieving. Let us pray that Tun Dr Mahathir and his family remain strong in facing this great ordeal,” he said. — Bernama

Title: ‘Dedicated lanes, smooth queues’: F1 fans praise improved crowd and traffic management at Sepang Circuit
Article:
SEPANG, Oct 3 — Formula 1 (F1) fans have praised the improved crowd and traffic management at the Sepang International Circuit (SIC) here today, following congestion and long queues reported after yesterday’s opening day of the Formula 1 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia 2026.
Several fans took to social media to highlight smoother queues, dedicated lanes for shuttle buses and a stronger presence of staff, marshals and police to manage crowds and traffic.
A Threads user, @tanissha_.26, commended the arrangements, particularly the dedicated lanes and improved coordination for shuttle buses.
“Good job on crowd control today. Smooth queue, no tug of war. Dedicated lane for shuttle buses. Shut off the exit for only shuttle buses, tons of crew, marshall, police, proper instructions and control
Thank you so much for taking in control,” the user said.
Another user, @edadoodle, praised the queue management and assistance provided by staff at the KLIA (Kuala Lumpur International Airport) Transit station and shuttle point.
“Thank you @malaysiaairports the line is super fast, so much bus queueing up for us and there’s a lot of staff guiding us from the KLIA Transit train station to the shuttle point. I lined up at 9.15am and already on the way to @sepangcircuit by 9.25am,” it said.
Meanwhile, @nnhs_nadhirah described today’s arrangements as more orderly compared with yesterday and hoped it will stay the same when they leave the venue later today.
Another visitor, @ryanmahowlett, also noted a significant improvement upon arriving at SIC this morning.
“Arrived at Sepang this morning. Much better organisation. Shuttle buses have their own dedicated lanes, lots of traffic police organising traffic, crowds a lot less. Much better,” it said.
The positive reactions came a day after social media users had earlier highlighted congestion upon leaving SIC, with some reporting lengthy waits for shuttle buses to parking areas and nearby transport hubs.
The reports prompted calls for more efficient traffic management, increased shuttle bus capacity and closer coordination of public transport services to handle the large crowds attending the event.
Meanwhile, a social media post showed SIC chief executive officer Azhan Shafriman Hanif on the ground earlier today, overseeing and assisting with the flow of buses to the iconic venue.
The Formula 1 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia 2026, which marks F1’s return to SIC for the first time since 2017, continues today with the final practice session and qualifying session before the 56-lap race tomorrow.
In July, Formula 1 confirmed Malaysia as the host of the Gulf Air Bahrain GP from Oct 2 to 4, following an agreement between Formula 1, the International Automobile Federation (FIA) and the governments of Malaysia and Bahrain.
The agreement keeps the Bahrain GP on the 2026 F1 calendar after the race was cancelled earlier this season due to geopolitical tensions in West Asia.
Malaysia hosted the Malaysian GP at SIC from 1999 to 2017 before the race was dropped from the F1 calendar. — Bernama

Title: Rapid KL: Sepang shuttle arrangements improved for Day 2 of Bahrain GP after feedback
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 3 — Rapid KL said it has improved shuttle bus arrangements at the Sepang International Circuit (SIC) today following complaints from Formula One spectators over long queues and delays yesterday.
Rapid KL said that as of 11am, traffic and passenger movements were smooth and under control, adding that it would continue monitoring the situation with SIC and the relevant agencies.
“Following the feedback received, Rapid KL together with SIC and the relevant agencies have made improvements to arrangements at the pick-up and drop-off locations,” it said in a statement.
“These improvements have been implemented from today to ensure smoother and more orderly passenger movements,” it added.
The public transport operator said it had taken note of passenger feedback over journeys to SIC yesterday and worked with the circuit and relevant agencies on the changes.
Rapid KL nevertheless said its shuttle services yesterday had operated as planned and in accordance with arrangements agreed with the event organisers, Bahrain International Circuit (BIC) and SIC.
It said its responsibilities included managing bus movements and passenger flows according to the agreed operating arrangements, while overall traffic coordination to and from SIC and vehicle movements around pick-up and drop-off areas were managed jointly with the organiser and relevant agencies.
The response follows complaints from spectators yesterday of severe congestion, disorganised shuttle queues and waits of several hours to leave the circuit after the first day of the Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia.
Rapid KL had earlier announced that 95 free shuttle buses would operate between SIC and KLIA Terminal 2, Mitsui Outlet Park and Bandar Baru Enstek, with buses scheduled every 10 to 15 minutes subject to traffic conditions.
The operator said it would continue working with all parties to improve coordination and passenger movements throughout the event.

Title: Malaysia to begin bringing Malbatt personnel home from Lebanon in January, says defence minister
Article:
KOTA TINGGI, Oct 3 — All members of the Malaysian Battalion (Malbatt) currently serving in Lebanon are expected to begin returning home in January 2027, following the conclusion of the United Nations Interim Force in Lebanon (Unifil) mandate at the end of this year.
Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said the withdrawal process for the personnel would be carried out in stages via several flights, followed by the return of military assets by sea starting January 17.
He noted that all battalions operating in Lebanon are scheduled to complete their respective deployments by the end of December, in line with the expiration of the mission’s mandate.
“Our personnel are expected to start returning next January on several flights, while Malaysian military assets will be brought back by ship starting January 17,” he said at a press conference following the groundbreaking ceremony for the Kota Tinggi Muslim Orphanage here today.
In a related development, the Kota Tinggi Member of Parliament expressed Malaysia’s readiness to consider participating in a new peacekeeping force in Lebanon should the United Nations (UN) request it.
However, he said this readiness is subject to the UN’s decision and the mandate provided, as Malaysia will not participate in any military operation that does not fall under the mandate of the world body.
“If the UN decides to establish a new force under whatever name and requires our involvement, Malaysia is prepared to participate.
“However, this is subject to the UN’s decision. We will not participate in any operation that does not fall under the mandate of the relevant world body,” he said.
Elaborating further, Mohamed Khaled said the matter was also addressed during his recent working visit to Lebanon, including in discussions with his counterpart, who indicated that the security situation in the country remains volatile and exposed to various threats.
He noted that a UN conference is currently underway, and many of the countries participating in the peacekeeping mission have expressed the view that the mission’s termination should be reviewed.
Recounting the history of the country’s involvement in Lebanon, Mohamed Khaled said Malaysian military participation began on a small scale in 2007 before the UN approved a full battalion-strength deployment in 2013. — Bernama

Title: Car pulled from river after plunging in, but 77-year-old driver still missing near Sungai Petani
Article:
SUNGAI PETANI, Oct 3 — A 77-year-old man remains missing after the car he was driving is believed to have skidded and plunged into a river along Jalan Lubuk Segintah-Lubuk Kawah near here early today.
Kuala Muda police chief ACP Hanyan Ramlan said that in the incident, which occurred at about 1am, Mat Yusof Hashim was believed to have been driving a Proton Wira from Jalan Kuala Ketil towards Felda Teloi Timur.
“The driver was initially believed to have drowned, but after the car was pulled out of the river using a crane, the victim was not in the vehicle.
“As such, the Fire and Rescue Department is continuing the search and rescue operation for the victim in the surrounding river area,” he said in a statement today.
He said the vehicle was found to have sustained extensive damage, especially to the front section and both doors, adding that the car had been towed to the Kuala Muda Traffic Police Station.
“The case is still under investigation and has yet to be classified,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Ranau records weak 3.5-magnitude earthquake, tremors felt in surrounding areas
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Oct 3 — A weak earthquake measuring 3.5 on the Richter scale occurred in the Panginatan area of ​​Ranau at 10.57am today.
The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) said the earthquake’s epicentre was detected at coordinates 5.9° North and 116.7° East, at a depth of 13 kilometres.
According to MetMalaysia, the epicentre was located approximately 14 kilometres south of Ranau.
“Tremors from the incident were reportedly felt by residents in the Ranau district and surrounding areas,” the department said.
MetMalaysia confirmed it would continue to closely monitor the situation following the earthquake.
Meanwhile, MetMalaysia has requested the public specifically those who felt the tremors to complete a questionnaire via the official link https://forms.gle/cYMVjU7DYeKBV3ZbA to assist in the collection of field data.
Ranau is a district in the interior of Sabah, located 106 kilometres east of Kota Kinabalu, and is home to Mount Kinabalu. — Bernama

Title: Khaled Nordin: PAS can discuss using BN logo for Melaka polls, but door not open to all Perikatan parties
Article:
KOTA TINGGI, Oct 3 — Umno wil be selective in permitting parties under Perikatan Nasional (PN) from using Barisan Nasional’s (BN) logo should they agree to a political cooperation for the upcoming Melaka state election, said party vice president Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin.
He said that only parties deemed acceptable would be allowed to use the BN logo, with only PAS having expressed such an intention
“We have not discussed the matter yet. PAS only expressed such a move to the press.
“This doesn’t mean we have actually agreed on PAS using the BN logo yet,” he told reporters after officiating a groundbreaking ceremony for an Islamic orphanage here today.
On the possibility of Parti Wawasan Negara (Wawasan) contesting under BN due to potential logo
restrictions following the Registrar of Societies’ (RoS) recent suspension of the coalition, Mohamed Khaled said BN and Umno welcomes any party that support the coalition.
However, he stressed that allowing any party to contest under the BN logo would be contingent on several fundamental decisions.
“As a house owner, who do we invite into our home? We don’t just invite anyone, except people that we sincerely like,” he said in reference to Umno being selective for other parties using BN’s logo.
Yesterday, PAS president Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang said the party was prepared to use the BN logo in the Melaka state election if an agreement on cooperation was reached.
He said PAS was open to using either its own logo or BN’s, depending on the outcome of negotiations.

Title: Army officer arrested at public university with firearm, preliminary test positive for ketum compound
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 3 — The Malaysian Army (TDM) has confirmed that all firearms and ammunition in its storage facilities are fully accounted for following the arrest of an army officer at a public university on September 28.
The Strategic Communications Branch of the Army Headquarters said today that immediate inspections of all armouries and storage facilities were conducted as soon as the force received information regarding the incident.
According to the statement, the officer was detained by the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) to assist in investigations after being found in possession of a firearm, a quantity of ammunition, and a liquid suspected to be a prohibited substance.
“An initial urine screening of the officer tested positive for Mitragynine however, this result remains subject to further confirmation through laboratory analysis and the outcome of the authorities’ investigation.
“TDM views the matters involving military personnel and officers seriously, particularly those concerning discipline, security, and adherence to regulations,” the statement read.
TDM reiterated its commitment to cooperating fully with the authorities and taking appropriate action should any regulatory violations be confirmed by the investigation findings.
“Any conclusions regarding the incident must be based on facts and the authorities’ investigation findings, rather than unverified information.
“TDM also urges the public to refrain from speculation or spreading information that could mislead the community and compromise the investigation process,” the statement added.
Further updates will be announced through official TDM channels at the appropriate time. — Bernama

Title: Negeri Sembilan seeks federal support for roads, water security and disaster preparedness in Budget 2027
Article:
SEREMBAN, Oct 3 — Strengthening critical infrastructure, boosting water security and enhancing disaster preparedness are among Negeri Sembilan’s key priorities put forward for the Federal Government’s consideration in Budget 2027.
Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim said the priorities also included measures to improve access to education and quality healthcare, while strengthening food security for the well-being of the people in the state.
Speaking to Bernama recently, he said the key priorities were identified based on the strategic importance of each project in driving economic growth, enhancing the well-being of the people and ensuring balanced development throughout the state.
On the transport sector, Ismail said road network development was essential to improving connectivity and facilitating the movement of people and goods, while providing direct access to industrial, logistics and new growth hubs.
He said Negeri Sembilan was seeking the Federal Government’s support to provide enabling infrastructure that could drive economic growth and investment while improving the well-being of the people.
Ismail said the state government was ready to work with the Federal Government through various ministries, departments and agencies to ensure the effective implementation, monitoring and evaluation of development projects and programmes for the benefit of the people.
He said Federal Government support would help lay a strong foundation for the state’s medium- and long-term development.
Detailing the needs by district, Ismail said Seremban and Port Dickson required significant infrastructure improvements to cater to rapid population growth and growing demand in the housing, industrial and mobility sectors.
As for Rembau, he said the focus was on expanding water supply capacity and improving health facilities, while Jempol would prioritise strengthening the rural economy and food security to ensure that development benefits reached all sections of society.
Ismail said the development proposals were in line with Negeri Sembilan’s long-term development plan for 2026-2035, which emphasises economic and social growth, sustainability and inclusive development.
Budget 2027 is scheduled to be tabled in Parliament on October 9. — Bernama

Title: MCMC: Meta confirms technical error wrongfully suspended WhatsApp accounts in Malaysia
Article:
CYBERJAYA, Oct 3 — Meta has acknowledged that a technical error in its system had caused legitimate WhatsApp user activity to be wrongly identified as rule violations, affecting more than half of the cases in the first batch submitted by the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC).
In a statement today, MCMC said it had received feedback from Meta regarding the issue of WhatsApp account suspensions that had previously been brought to the company’s attention.
“According to Meta, the technical error was addressed at the end of September and affected legitimate accounts were proactively restored, including some accounts that had not submitted appeals.
“Meta also confirmed that no changes had been made to its enforcement policies or WhatsApp Terms of Service,” the statement said.
MCMC said that for other cases, Meta explained that account suspensions could involve several factors, including recycled phone numbers previously associated with blocked accounts, spam or scam activity, and usage patterns detected by WhatsApp’s security systems.
According to the statement, user reports are one of the factors assessed and are not the sole basis for account suspension.
Regarding business accounts, Meta said sending messages without consent or in high volumes, particularly to recipients who are not on the contact list, could be detected as spam activity.
“Business users are advised to obtain recipients’ consent before sending messages in bulk,” the statement said.
Meanwhile, MCMC has asked Meta to improve its appeal and recovery processes so that affected users receive confirmation, information on the status of their review, and clearer and faster action.
MCMC advised affected users to use WhatsApp’s official appeal and support channels.
“MCMC will continue to monitor the resolution of outstanding cases and ensure that improvements are implemented to facilitate users in regaining access to their accounts.
“Further regulatory action will be considered if Meta’s measures are found to be inadequate,” it said. — Bernama

Title: Banks and insurers ready to offer relief to families affected by Nepal-China floods, says BNM
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 3 — Financial service providers stand ready to extend appropriate relief and support to the families of the victims affected by the recent floods along the Nepal-China border, in line with applicable laws and regulatory requirements, said Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM).
The central bank said that assistance or goodwill measures may include repayment deferments, waivers of fees and charges, and flexibility in documentation requirements pending the completion of the relevant legal processes.
“Financial institutions may also prioritise the processing and validation of policy or certificate status, expedite the payment of insurance and takaful claims, as well as provide other forms of support tailored to the specific needs of the affected families,” it told Bernama in a statement.
BNM advised next of kin of the affected Malaysians to reach out to the relevant financial institutions for appropriate assistance. The central bank said it will work closely with financial institutions to ensure the timely provision of support to those impacted by the tragedy. — Bernama

Title: Perak floods displace 58 people, two relief centres opened
Article:
IPOH, Oct 3 — Two temporary relief centres (PPS) have been opened in Perak to house 58 people from 17 families affected by floods in the Hilir Perak, and Larut, Matang and Selama districts.
The State Disaster Management Committee Secretariat said all the victims had been placed at the PPS at Dewan Orang Ramai Kampung Degong in Hilir Perak and the PPS at Kampung Menteri Mosque in Larut, Matang and Selama.
“The PPS at Dewan Orang Ramai Kampung Degong is sheltering three victims following floods in the Jalan Kampar-Langkap area at 4pm last Thursday.
“The PPS at Kampung Menteri Mosque, meanwhile, is sheltering 55 victims from 15 families following floods in the Kampung Menteri area at 8pm yesterday,” it said in a statement today.
Meanwhile, the Malaysian Meteorological Department has forecast thunderstorms in Hulu Perak, Kuala Kangsar, Kinta, Kampar, Batang Padang and Muallim this afternoon, with rain expected tonight. — Bernama

Title: Man killed, family injured in Port Dickson crash involving lorry driver allegedly over alcohol limit
Article:
PORT DICKSON, Oct 3 — A man was killed while his wife and daughter were injured after the Perodua Myvi they were travelling in collided with a lorry driven by a man suspected to be under the influence of alcohol at KM13.5 of Jalan Lukut-Sepang here yesterday.
Port Dickson district police chief Supt Ahmad Afiq Mohd Adnan said the 35-year-old car driver died at the scene due to severe injuries in the 6.50pm incident, while his 32-year-old wife and their five-year-old daughter sustained injuries.
He said preliminary investigations found that the accident occurred when the 46-year-old lorry driver, who was travelling in the Lukut-Sepang direction, is believed to have lost control of the vehicle before entering the opposite lane and colliding with the car.
“The lorry driver was unhurt. An initial screening found that his urine test was negative, but a breathalyser test showed an alcohol reading above the permitted limit. All the victims were taken to Port Dickson Hospital for further action,” he said in a statement today.
He said the lorry driver had been arrested and the case was being investigated under Section 44(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987. — Bernama

Title: Malaysian listed as ‘uncontactable’ after Nepal floods returns home safely, 54 still missing
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 3 — A Malaysian previously reported as uncontactable following floods and landslides in Nepal has returned safely to Malaysia, the Foreign Ministry said today.
The ministry said the individual presented himself at the Malaysian Embassy in Kathmandu on October 1, where officials verified his identity and confirmed that he was safe, before he returned to Malaysia yesterday.
“Following his return, the relevant authorities in Malaysia will record a statement from the individual to complete the official record concerning his case,” it said in a statement.
“The individual will also undergo a health assessment,” it added.
The Malaysian Embassy in Kathmandu is meanwhile carrying out further checks with Nepalese authorities and reviewing relevant records following the development.
“With his status now confirmed, the Ministry’s record stands at 54 Malaysians reported as uncontactable,” Wisma Putra said.
The ministry said it would continue verifying each case separately and would not disclose further details about the Malaysian who returned, citing his privacy.
It said Nepal’s National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority announced on September 30 that search-and-rescue operations had ended and transitioned to search-and-recovery efforts.
Wisma Putra stressed that the transition would not end Malaysia’s efforts to establish the status of the 54 Malaysians, with verification continuing through its embassies in Kathmandu and Beijing, relevant authorities and other official channels.
The Malaysians were reported uncontactable after devastating floods and debris flows struck Nepal and parts of neighbouring Tibet on August 26.
The disaster, linked to glacial ice and rock collapses in the upper catchment of Lhende Khola in Tibet, was reported to have killed more than 1,450 people, with thousands more unaccounted for.

Title: Malaysia eyes role in Brazilian aircraft maker Embraer’s global supply chain
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 3 — Malaysia is exploring cooperation with Embraer Defense & Security of Brazil to join the company’s regional and global supply chain.
Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said the matter was discussed during a courtesy call by the company’s chief commercial officer, Frederico Lemos, at Wisma Pertahanan yesterday.
He said Embraer has expertise in aircraft development and integrated defence solutions.
“This meeting paves the way to explore collaboration in developing the local downstream ecosystem and opportunities for Malaysia to participate in Embraer’s supply chain at regional and global levels.
“This potential aligns with the aspirations of the National Defence Industry Policy (DIPN) to strengthen the capabilities of the local defence industry,” he said in a Facebook post. — Bernama

Title: Four areas in Johor and Sarawak still in unhealthy API range, Sri Aman highest at 152
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 3 — Four areas in Johor and Sarawak recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 9am today.
According to data from the Department of Environment’s (DOE) Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS), Sri Aman in Sarawak recorded the highest reading at 152, followed by Pasir Gudang, Johor (151).
The other affected areas were IPD Serian in Sarawak (126) and Larkin, Johor (121).
Meanwhile, 61 areas recorded moderate readings, while two areas were classified as having favourable air quality - Taiping, Perak (44) and Temerloh, Pahang (42).
The API reading for the Kota Kinabalu, Sabah station was unavailable at the time.
API readings of 0 to 50 are classified as good, 51 to 100 as moderate, 101 to 200 as unhealthy, 201 to 300 as very unhealthy, and above 300 as hazardous. — Bernama

Title: Bahrain GP in Malaysia: F1 fans complain of gridlocked traffic, over three-hour waits for shuttles
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 3 — Formula 1 spectators have complained of gridlocked roads, long shuttle bus queues and poor crowd management at the Sepang International Circuit (SIC), after the first day of the Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia yesterday.
Malaysian X user @tuakdotsol, said this morning that roads heading towards the circuit remained gridlocked, while private cars and e-hailing vehicles were apparently being stopped at the perimeter, funnelling spectators towards shuttle hubs at Mitsui Outlet Park and KLIA Terminal 2.
“Apparently private cars and Grabs are blocked at the perimeter, so everyone funnels into shuttle hubs at Mitsui outlet and KLIA T2,” the user wrote, alongside images showing large crowds near the circuit.
British content creator Ryan Howlett, who is based in Malaysia, said he left Sepang at 5.45pm yesterday but only managed to board a bus at 9pm, describing the experience as “one of the craziest things” he had encountered.
Howlett also alleged that people were fighting, shouting and throwing objects at buses amid the crowds, while criticising what he described as an absence of signs or information when spectators exited the circuit.
Another X user, @saroki19, described the journey from Sepang to KLIA yesterday as “very bad” and “horrendous”, criticising the organisation of the shuttle service and traffic management.
“Really need to think & plan this well. Sunday is going to be hell!” the user wrote, while tagging Rapid KL, the police and KLIA Ekspres.
Malaysian X user @RimauXI also complained yesterday of “super long” bus queues, while noting that access to the circuit from the Sultan Abdul Samad KLIA Mosque roundabout was restricted to authorised vehicles.
The complaints come despite extensive transport arrangements announced ahead of the race, with Rapid KL saying 95 free shuttle buses would run every 10 to 15 minutes from KLIA Terminal 2, Mitsui Outlet Park and Bandar Baru Enstek between 7am and midnight, although frequencies were subject to traffic conditions.
KLIA had warned that more than 200,000 spectators were expected over the three-day event, with daily crowds potentially exceeding 100,000, and advised racegoers to use public transport because of limited parking and expected congestion.
The Bahrain Grand Prix is being held at Sepang from October 2 to 4 after the original Bahrain race could not go ahead, bringing Formula 1 back to the Malaysian circuit for the first time since 2017.
